case_name: Reserve Coverage Test — Full Backing Article 36(1)

computation.tail_convention: LOW-tail for coverage: the WORST-CASE for the issuer is reserve_value BEING LOW relative to supply. The test compares coverage_ratio to the 100% threshold; coverage_ratio >= 1.0 PASSES (right tail — high coverage — is favourable).

result.regulatory_verdict: ADEQUATE — Article 36(1) full-backing requirement met (reserve 102% of supply).
result.test_anchor: MiCA Article 36(1) — reserve of assets equal to at least the outstanding token supply at all times.

article_basis: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, Article 36(1) — issuers of asset-referenced tokens (ART) must maintain a reserve of assets whose value is at least equal to the outstanding token supply.
tail_convention: Adverse tail for coverage = LOW tail of (reserve/supply). High coverage is favourable. Test examines whether coverage_ratio >= 100% under the issuer-stressed scenario (lower reserve_value, higher supply_value).
weakest_point: The supply and reserve values are point-in-time. MiCA Article 36 imposes AT-ALL-TIMES coverage; a single snapshot satisfying 102% does not establish the at-all-times condition. No liquidity, no segregation, no custody-quality check is performed here.

inputs.pct_of_reserve_used: UNKNOWN-CURRENT-VALUE — parameterised; MiCA Article 35 specifies own funds equal to the HIGHER of (i) a percentage of the reserve assets and (ii) a fixed EUR minimum; current statutory percentages are NOT cited here because not verified to source.

computation.tail_convention: Adverse tail for own-funds adequacy = LOW tail of own_funds_held. Own_funds_held >= MAX(pct_of_reserve, fixed_min) PASSES; high own-funds held is favourable.

result.regulatory_verdict: ADEQUATE — own funds held (380k) >= required MAX(20.4k, 350k) = 350k.
result.test_anchor: MiCA Article 35 — own-funds requirement for ART issuers (higher of percentage-of-reserve and fixed minimum).

article_basis: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, Article 35 — own-funds requirement for issuers of asset-referenced tokens.
tail_convention: Adverse tail = LOW tail of own. Test examines whether own_funds_held is at least MAX(pct_of_reserve_amount, fixed_minimum).
weakest_point: PCT_OF_RESERVE_ART and the fixed-minimum amount are parameterised as named constants because the current statutory percentages were not independently verified against the consolidated MiCA text in this environment. The chosen illustrative values (2%, 350k EUR) are placeholders. A real computation requires citation of the actual Article 35 figures as published in the Official Journal.

case_name: Stressed Coverage Test — Haircuts on Reserve

inputs.haircut_convention: applied to reserve assets; LOW tail of reserve is the issuer-adverse scenario

computation.shortfall_EUR: tail_converse tail for coverage = LOW tail of (stressed_reserve / supply). The stress INCREASES the issuer's adverse tail by marking down reserve_value. Coverage_pct 96.9% is the issuer-adverse outcome, not the favourable one.

result.regulatory_verdict: INADEQUATE under Article 36( stressed reserve 96.9% of supply breaches the 100% full-backing requirement; shortfall 31k EUR.
result.test_anchor: MiCA Article 36(1) — full-backing tested under issuer-adverse (LOW-tail) reserve haircut.

article_basis: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, Article 36(1) full-backing requirement re-tested under a reserve-asset haircut.
tail_convention: Adverse tail for coverage = LOW tail of reserve_value/supply_value. The haircut shifts reserve_value into the LOW tail (issuer-adverse). The test examines whether the LOW-tail outcome still satisfies the 100% threshold.
weakest_point: The 5% haircut is an illustrative stress; MiCA does not specify a single stress magnitude for ART reserves. Asset-class-specific haircuts (per delegated acts and Article 36 custodial-quality rules) would be required for a real capital assessment. The stress test as stated is a one-factor parallel haircut — concentration risk, duration mismatch, and FX risk are not modelled.

case_name: Redemption at Par — Article 39 Obligation Math

inputs.liquidity_bucket_EUR: HQLA-equivalent available within the redemption window

computation.tail_convention: Adverse tail for redemption = LOW tail of (liquidity_bucket / redemption_obligation). Adequate liquidity is liquidity_bucket >= redemption_obligation; HIGH liquidity is favourable.

result.regulatory_verdict: ADEQUATE — Article 39 redemption-at-par obligation can be met; liquidity bucket (120k) exceeds obligation (50k); post-redemption reserve coverage 102.1% still meets Article 36(1).
result.test_anchor: MiCA Article 39 (redemption at par) and Article 36(1) (full-backing retained post-redemption).

article_basis: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, Article 39 (redemption at par on holder request) and Article 36(1) (continuous full-backing).

tailAdverse tail for redemption-capacity = LOW tail of liquidity_bucket / redemption_obligation. The test examines whether liquidity_bucket is in the LOW tail (issuer-adverse) still >= obligation; and whether post-redemption reserve_value remains >= post-redemption supply.
weakest_point: A single redemption request of 50k units does Article 39's stress assumptions. MiCA permits temporary suspension only in strictly defined circumstances (Article 39(3)); the case ignores concentration of redemption timing. Coverage post-redemption improves mechanically because reserve and supply contract by the same amount, but a HIGH-CONCENTRATION redemption could deplete the liquidity bucket below the obligation.
